newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to slowly reduce sugar beet sowing-Ag Min.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to slowly reduce sugar beet sowing-Ag Min.

text.p: Ukraine planned to reduce the area sown to sugar beet to 800,000-900,000 hectares in the next few years from about 1.3 million hectares sown in previous years, the deputy prime minister of agriculture said on Friday.

"We no longer need to sow 1.3 to 1.4 million hectares to sugar beets, and in the next few years the maximum area will be at 800,000 to 900,000 hectares," Mykhailo Zubets, also the Agriculture Minister, told an agriculture conference.
Zubets said Ukraine needs to rescue its sugar market because it no longer has the export outlets to justify continuing at recent rates of production.
Ukraine produced 3.26 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 crop year and 3.49 million in 1995/96, mostly from its own sugarbeet crops plus imported raws.
It planted 1.347 million hectares with sugar beet last year, down from 1995's 1.406 million.

Recent restrictions placed on Ukrainian exports to other former Soviet republics like Russia and Belarus, traditionally major outlets for its refined sugar, have left Ukraine with an oversupply on the domestic market.
Both neighbouring countries have accused Ukraine of dumping cheap sugar on their markets.
Zubets repeated earlier statements that the government would impose price quotas on the local market by doubling domestic prices, and limit the amount it exported abroad.
He did not say how much refined sugar Ukraine expected to produce this year.
